TERMS & CONDITIONS OF EMPLOYMENT

1. Documents and Evaluation:

Within three business days of your first day of work, you must submit a copy of your Secondary School Certificate mark sheet, a copy of the mark sheet of the last professional exam passed and a copy of your Aadhar and PAN card including relieving letter and salary slips/certificates from the last employer.

If an Employee is unable to produce the required documentation or a letter requesting the appropriate documentation within three days of hire, employment will be terminated at the will of the management.

2. Office Timing:

Office hours for staff are 9:00 AM to 6:00 PM and factory workers are 9:00 AM to 7:00 PM, with a 15-minute margin. Latecomers will be marked half-day.

3. Absence:

Absence for a continuous period of four days without prior approval of your superior, (including overstay of leave/training), can lead to your services being terminated without notice or explanation.

4. Probation Period:

4.1 The probationary period will normally last for 6 calendar months during which time the manager will meet regularly with the probationer to discuss their progress and suitability to the role.

4.2 For Trainees, the probation period will start with post successful completion of their training period.

4.3 If there are any concerns about the probationer's suitability or if there has been insufficient time to assess the probationer due to their absence, the probationary period may be extended for up to one calendar month or for a reasonable period that allows the probationer to be properly assessed. This extension will only be considered appropriate if the manager believes that the probationer has the potential to meet the required standards within this additional time period.

4.4 At any time during your probation period the Company may confirm your employment by way of a written communication if your performance is found to be satisfactory.

4.5 During the probation period, the company reserves the right to relieve you immediately without any notice period, in case of any breach of the Employment Agreement or for any other reasons as determined by the Company.

4.6 During the probation period, your employment with the Company may be terminated:

  • a. by you, upon giving the Company two one month’s written notice or at the Company’s discretion payment of gross salary in lieu of notice;
  • b. by the Company, upon giving you one month’s written notice or payment of gross salary in lieu thereof.

5. Code of Conduct:

Every organization has certain expectations from employees in terms of their behaviour and conduct while working in the office. All employees are required to follow this code of conduct.

A code of conduct is required to maintain a healthy, safe working environment for all employees.

Company Core Values:

  • Accountability
  • Commitment
  • Quality

Critical Success Factors/ Core Competencies:

  • Customer Centricity
  • Result Orientation
  • Operational
  • Excellence/Speed of Execution
  • Accountability/Ownership
  • Teamwork & Collaboration
  • Creativity & Innovation
  • Continuous Learning & Growth

All employees should exhibit company values and core competencies in their day to day behavior/conduct.

The following behaviors are not acceptable from any employee:

  • A. Disrespect for our Employees
  • B. Drug & Alcohol Abuse/ Smoking
  • C. Sexual & Other Unlawful Harassment
  • D. Fraud and Theft
  • E. Neglect of job responsibilities or unsatisfactory performance

Any form of harassment of our employees will not be tolerated. This includes inappropriate verbal or physical or visual conduct, offensive, abusive or hostile work environment. The unwelcome behavior includes those that are:

  • Humiliating
  • Unsafe
  • Unhealthy
  • Discriminatory
  • Career limiting
  • Intimidating

Violation of the Code of Conduct:

All employees are expected to strictly adhere to the principles outlined in the Code of Conduct. Since the Code of Conduct cannot cover every conceivable situation confronting employees in the conduct of their daily business, employees are advised to use their common sense and judgment in extending and applying these principles and to seek advice from their management in cases of doubt, or for necessary clarification.

In the event of a violation of any of the clauses of the code of conduct, strict disciplinary action will be taken against an employee and if required it may lead to termination of employment without notice. Employee shall be liable for all damages, including actual damages and lost profits, caused to the Company, as well as termination of employment without notice. An employee shall allow the Company to adjust and/or recover such damages from the dues payable to him/her by the Company.

6. Confidentiality and Other Terms:

Whilst employed by the company:

  • (a) You will not be allowed to undertake any other employment or engage in any external activities of a commercial nature without prior written approval of your manager.
  • (b) Except on the proper course of your appointment, or, thereafter you shall not divulge to any third party any information regarding the affairs or business matters of the company or information regarding its clients, business associates or customers without prior approval. All information that comes to your knowledge by reasons of your employment with the company is deemed to be confidential.
  • (c) During working hours, an employee shall not indulge in any other activities with any other company or person who may cause harm to the employer either in the form of financial liabilities or against the business reputation of the Company. Also, after working hours the employee will neither use any kinds of assets of the Company nor the name of the company in any way other than for the benefit of the Company.
  • (d) Further the employee will not indulge in any other activities which may call for civil/criminal liabilities to this company on account of his illegal or unethical activities.
  • (e) No one is permitted to remove or make copies of any records, reports or documents without prior Management approval. Disclosure of confidential information could lead to termination, as well as other possible legal action.

In the event of any above things happening, all the liabilities either pecuniary or otherwise will be entirely of the employee. Even in the event of a loss of confidence of the company upon you, it will be the sufficient ground for the Company to terminate your employment with immediate effect. The Company in no case will be liable to the parties to such illegal or unethical act of the employees.

7. Non-Compete, Non-Solicit AND EXCLUSIVITY:

You categorically agree that during the subsistence of your employment and for a period of 1 year after termination or separation from the company/or during your notice period you shall not, for any reason whatsoever participate or render services directly or indirectly, in any company engaged in similar to or compete with the business of the company. May it be clear that under no circumstances, if any employee communicates directly or indirectly with any of the company's clientele then legal action will be taken.

You shall not for the duration of your employment, and for the period thereafter, solicit directly or indirectly with the customers, employees, consultants and contractors of the Company for your own interest.

8. Leave:

You will be entitled to 12 Earned leaves & 6 Casual leaves in a year, which will be applicable after completing your probation period. This would be apart from the national holidays and festivals. For further details refer to the leave policy.

9. Duties and Obligations:

  • (a) Abide by all Company's rules, regulations, policies, procedures framed by the Company from time to time and applicable to the position which may include without limitation matters of conduct, behavior, discipline, working hours, and other duties and obligations.
  • (b) Immediately upon your knowledge, inform the Company of any act of dishonesty or any action prejudicial to the interests of the Company on the part of any other employee of the Company.

10. Performance Evaluations:

The Company may conduct periodic performance reviews. The performance evaluations may vary depending on the length of service, job position, past performance, changes in job duties, or recurring performance problems. During your performance evaluations, your Supervisor may review factors such as the quality and quantity of the work you perform, your knowledge of the job, your initiative, your work attitude, and your attitude toward others. The performance evaluations are intended to make you aware of any progress, areas for improvement, and objectives or goals for future work performance. A positive performance evaluation does not guarantee an increase in salary or promotion.

11. Work Eligibility:

  1. Your appointment is based on the assumption that you have never been charged with any criminal offence under the Indian Penal Code or any other law in force. If any such information comes to light, your employment will be terminated automatically.
  2. Your appointment is subject to your being fit physically and mentally to carry out the functions assigned to you.
  3. Any physical disability or disease should be disclosed to the Company prior to your employment, else it would result in your termination.
  4. You agree to indemnify and hold the Company harmless from any and all claims, liabilities, losses, actions, damages, and the like arising from or in connection with any negligent or intentional acts or omissions on your part.

12. Termination:

  1. Your services may be terminated by either party, giving notice in writing for 4 weeks or payment of Total CTC in lieu thereof. The Company reserves the right to terminate your employment on any grounds whatsoever, including misconduct, unsatisfactory performance, or refusal to comply with lawful directives, without notice or payment in lieu.
  2. In case the employee resigns, he/she will not be eligible for any accrued incentives and variable component pay for current or previous months.
  3. Proper handover of Company property is mandatory. All belongings in your custody (e.g., mobile phones, laptop, sim card, keys, passwords, documents, etc.) must be returned safely without copying or extracting any part of them.
  4. The Company is entitled to deduct any claims from the Employee's emoluments. Full and final settlement, if any, will be processed 30 days from the date of separation.
  5. Termination due to death will be effective as of the date of death.
    • Upon notification of death, the manager should inform HR immediately.
    • The HR/Finance team will process beneficiary payments as per benefits plans.

6. Immediate Termination

The Company may terminate employment with immediate effect under the following circumstances:

  1. If an act by the employee is detrimental to the Company’s interest.
  2. Guilty of dishonesty, disobedience, disorderly behavior, negligence, insubordination, unauthorized absence, or any conduct harmful to the Company’s interest.
  3. Performance remains unsatisfactory even after warnings.
  4. If the Management suspects the integrity of the employee or loses confidence in them.

Upon termination, all documents and property entrusted to the employee must be immediately returned.

13. Complaints:

The Company follows an open-door policy. Employees are encouraged to report concerns to their immediate Supervisor or HR. We want all employees to feel comfortable raising issues to help maintain a positive workplace.

14. Personal Data:

Employees must inform the Company of any changes to personal data including address, phone number, and emergency contact information to comply with legal requirements.

15. Governing Law and Jurisdiction:

Any disputes shall be governed by Indian laws and subject to the jurisdiction of courts in New Delhi.

16. Review/Amendments/Modifications/Withdrawal:

This document is subject to change. Any modifications must be approved by the Director/Management and will be communicated in writing. The Company’s decisions shall be final and binding.
